title: The Market is about to GO INSANE‼️

steps.does: Opens a brokerage app screenshot of the public account at the start and reads the account value, today's dollar and percent gain, and the 3-year rate of return chart.
steps.why: To report the day's result to viewers and show long-run account progress before moving to market topics.
steps.conclusion: Account up about $15,000 on the day, a strong 3-year return.

steps.does: Reads out the Nasdaq's October return for each year since 2008 from an open browser tab titled Nasdaq October returns, going year by year from -18% in 2008 to about +5% in 2025.
steps.why: To show that October is historically volatile with big swings both ways, so viewers should be ready for large moves and buying opportunities.
steps.conclusion: October is crazy in the market, a golden month for opportunities, especially smaller caps of $3-20 billion that can move 2-4x the index.

rules.text: A 5% Nasdaq move means many individual stocks make 10-20% moves within the same month.

steps.does: Plays a Bloomberg Television YouTube clip of Ed Yardeni on bond yields, then a Dan Ives clip on AI and tech stocks, pausing to react to each; later reacts to an AMD CEO interview.
steps.why: To gather Wall Street views on yields and tech and give his own counterview, framing the macro backdrop for his audience.
data: Yardeni not convinced 5.25% is the top in yields, possible 5.5-6%
Oil prices drive inflation fears and yields
Dan Ives on AI buildout and Anthropic IPO hype
steps.conclusion: Yields follow oil: if oil keeps rising yields keep rising, if oil chills yields fall; companies going public build hype to maximise valuation.

rules.text: Oil is the whole story for yields: oil up means yields up, oil down means yields down.
Companies going public have a job to build as much hype as possible to get a big valuation.
